weather_reasons: NWS hourly forecast includes thunderstorm potential
Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 202358
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
458 PM MST Thu Aug 20 2026

.UPDATE...Updated 00z Aviation Discussion...

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- After a brief reprieve from the extreme heat today over south- 
  central and eastern Arizona, highs will return to around 110 
  degrees by Friday, lasting into early next week. 

- Extreme Heat Warnings are in effect through Sunday evening due to 
  continued areas of high-end moderate to major HeatRisk.

- Isolated thunderstorms are expected across the AZ high terrain
  this afternoon and evening with less than 10% chances for the 
  lower deserts. Chances will likely remain confined to the high 
  terrain through at least Saturday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
After the biggest monsoon event of the season so far in the 
Phoenix Metro area, we are not anticipating much if any activity 
in the lower deserts today due to an overturned atmosphere. Latest
visible satellite and composite radar imagery reveals a remnant 
MCV left over from last night's storm complex which is now 
progressing through the Yuma area. This MCV is expected to 
continue bringing an area of light to moderate showers with a few 
embedded lightning strikes to Yuma and Imperial Counties over the 
next few hours before finally dissipating. Farther east, skies 
have cleared out across southcentral AZ allowing temperatures to 
begin rising, however highs in the Phoenix area will likely top 
out right around normal due to residual moisture from previous 
rainfall. Therefore, NBM high temperatures were adjusted down by 
several degrees this afternoon and overnight lows tonight as well.
Latest RAP 13 mesoanalysis across southcentral AZ shows CAPE 
values are still around 1000-1200 J/kg, but there is a much 
stronger mid-lvl inversion today with ML CIN on the order -120 
to -150 J/kg. Therefore storm coverage will be much more isolated
this afternoon, and without a strong outflow, little to no storms
are expected across the lower deserts this afternoon and evening.

Deterministic models and ensemble members suggest the subtropical
high will shift over Colorado on Friday and then migrate into 
eastern NM on Saturday. This shift in the upper-lvl pattern will 
cause winds to turn more out of the south, ushering drier air into
our beginning on Friday. Both the GEFS and ECS show PWATs falling
to 1.3" or lower and mixing ratios as low as 7-8 g/kg. As such, 
NBM PoPs for both Friday and Saturday fall below 10% for the lower
deserts to 10-20% over portions of the high terrain. Despite 
storm coverage decreasing substantially, there will still be a 
chance of a distant outflow from storms along the International 
Border reaching Maricopa or Pinal Counties, but additional storm 
development is unlikely. Although the ridge axis will shift ewd 
into this weekend, overall 500 mb hght fields will remain largely 
unchanged from previous days. Therefore, we should see a return of
above normal temperatures and extreme heat conditions by Friday 
and persisting into this weekend and the Extreme Heat Warning will
remain in effect through Sunday.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Model uncertainty remains quite high for the first half of next
week as the position of the high is likely to set up somewhere
over eastern New Mexico and western Texas by Monday with little to
no movement into the middle of next week. This position can cause
higher uncertainty in moisture levels for our area with the 
latest guidance trying to advect some moisture into our area by 
Sunday or Monday, but NBM forecast PoPs are at most 10-15% for the
lower deserts. At this point, we could continue to see mostly 
slight chances favoring the high terrain into early next week, but
if moisture does eventually improve enough storm chances are 
likely to be higher than what the NBM is depicting. Another 
wildcard will be the potential influence of an upper level trough 
that may attempt to move into western portions of our region 
Sunday into Monday. If this occurs, it may be enough to improve 
convective potential across southeast California and western 
Arizona for Sunday and/or Monday. 

Temperatures are expected to continue to be more influenced by the
strong subtropical high as H5 heights hover between 593-596dm
across the Desert Southwest through early next week. Daytime highs
are not expected to change much day to day from Sunday through
early next, barring any significant change with the convective
chances. The Extreme Heat Warning is currently in effect through
Sunday, but it seems quite likely it will need to be extended 
again at some point.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2355Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major aviation weather concerns are expected through Friday
afternoon under FEW-SCT mid/high cloud decks. The main uncertainty
this evening will be whether or not a northeasterly outflow from
convection over the high terrain will propagate into the
terminals. At this time, a TEMPO group, mainly between the 03-07z
timeframe remains in place for the northeasterly shift with no
significant gusts expected this time. However, there is potential
that the outflow dissipates before making into the terminals and
thus westerly wind component continues a bit longer before the
eventual easterly shift overnight tonight. Otherwise, the overall
wind speeds will remain aob 10 kts. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major aviation weather concerns are expected through Friday
afternoon under FEW-SCT mid/high cloud decks. A remnant convective
complex is currently moving through Imperial County with just a
few high-based showers/sprinkles near the vicinity of KIPL. The 
activity should be moving west of KIPL within the next couple of 
hours. Otherwise, the overall wind pattern should behave similarly
to the last couple of days with winds fluctuating between the 
southwest to southeast with overall speeds aob 12 kts. Periods of 
light variability are likely during the early morning hours. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Elevated moisture levels will persist today with a temporary
reprieve from the extreme heat across much of the area. Expect 
mainly isolated showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and 
early evening over the AZ high terrain, with a less than 10%
chance of storms in the lower deserts. Drier air will filter into
the region Friday and Saturday with even lower chances for rain 
while temperatures heat back up to extreme levels. MinRHs of 
20-30% today will lower to 15-25% beginning Friday. Winds should 
overall follow the typical diurnal tendencies with some modest 
afternoon upslope gustiness.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Sunday for AZZ530>544-546-
     548>551-553>555-559-560.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT Sunday for CAZ562-565>567-
     569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Salerno
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...Lojero
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman/Salerno
